Separately, _validate_llm_response() (llm_backend.py:527) -- the prompt-echo/refusal guard meant to catch exactly this class of leak -- only checks for LEAKED ENGLISH rule text (_words() extracts [a-z0-9]+ and compares against the English system prompt's own rule lines). trs "Lutfen cevir" ("please translate") is a TARGET-LANGUAGE leak, so the English-only overlap check cannot catch it -- a real gap, not proof of the root cause. RECURRENCE (2026-09-08): confirmed at the identical structural position across 20+ languages on this ONE page -- the 'Text Frames with FrameFormat' paragraph describes properties with the pattern 'X and Y ... report Z' (plural subject, bare verb form 'report', no -s), and the bare verb is mistranslated as an IMPERATIVE command instead of 3rd-person-plural-indicative. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via live extraction trace (TextUnitExtractor.extract_from_ast on the real source file): the paragraph's single italic emphasis marker ('*current*') forces the ENTIRE paragraph into leaf-level extraction (_has_inline_formatting), fragmenting it at every code-span boundary. The bare-verb fragment ends up with NO visible subject (e.g. the unit is literally ', report where it is anchored relative to the page, margin, column, or paragraph; and' -- the subject 'HorizontalPosition and VerticalPosition, together with...' lives in separate CODE_SPAN units before it). English 'report' (bare form) is genuinely ambiguous between imperative and 3rd-person-plural without a visible subject; 'reports' (unambiguous -s form, e.g. 'IsFrame reports...') translates correctly in every locale for direct comparison. Thai is the only reviewed locale unaffected because it has no imperative/indicative mood distinction -- strong confirmation this is a genuine grammatical-ambiguity bug, not model variance. ARCHITECTURAL CONTEXT: this is the same class of bug TC-APT-013 (code spans) and TC-APT-036/076 (links) already fixed by excluding those inline elements from the leaf-splitting trigger in _has_inline_formatting; emphasis/bold appears to be the one common inline element NOT yet excluded. Those fixes each required a preserve_pattern + identity-round-trip validation across real pages before landing -- do not attempt the analogous emphasis exclusion without the same rigor (this note explicitly declines to guess at that fix). See data/summaries/fp-wave19-frameformat-imperative-verb-20260908.json for the full trace.

UPDATE to manual-wave24-blog-words-rb006-ar-enterprise-product and manual-wave24-blog-words-rb006-enterprise-product-multi-locale: the config/terminology.yaml fix (b801f275) was REVERTED this iteration (commit follows this one) after reverification against the exact originally-failing files surfaced a worse regression than the defect it fixed. Reverification manifest wave24-heal-words-rb006-reverify-20260909-r2 (ar/hu/ja/ro, professionalize_llm primary + m2m100 escalation) rejected ALL 4 cells with write_gate.py OVERWRITE BLOCKED: "Both existing (en) and new (en) are wrong language. Expected ar" -- i.e. the output came back predominantly/entirely English, not just the Enterprise-Product phrase. Root cause of the SIDE EFFECT (traced via a single-cell debug run with full stderr capture, not guessed): src/translation_engine/governed_terms.py::governed_multiword_terms() reads config/terminology.yaml exact_matches AUTOMATICALLY and feeds it into the language-detection signal-stripping used by write_gate.py's overwrite-comparison AND (per its own docstring) the frontmatter technical-signal regexes -- adding 5 new terms there did more than register a validator rule, it also changed what counts as "language evidence" for these short link-text units. The existing "Document Object Model" precedent comment in the same file explicitly warns terminology.yaml ALONE is validation-only and is NOT sufficient for actual pre-translation masking ("the profile pattern alone demonstrably does not hold" / needs a PAIRED site-profile preserve_pattern) -- I registered the new terms in terminology.yaml but did not add the paired preserve_pattern, so the terms were never actually masked from the model, while simultaneously being stripped from language- evidence text, which is the worse of both worlds for a short, term-dominated text unit like this one. NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: implement BOTH halves together (site-profile preserve_pattern for actual masking, matching the Document Object Model pattern exactly) and reverify with a full run BEFORE trusting it, the same discipline that caught this one. Do not re-add the terminology.yaml-only entries without the paired preserve_pattern -- reproduced this exact regression once already, no need to rediscover it.

Computed sha256 of every 3-gram in the actual English source and matched all 5 of the failing payload_sha256 hashes exactly: 74315251109ca6fa='3d for net' (source count=2), plus 4 more, ALL from one place -- the '## See Also' section's link '[Aspose.3D for .NET — Enterprise Documentation](https://docs.aspose.com/3d/net/)', which appears ONCE in source. The original LinkValidator warning already said it plainly: source_count=2, translation_count=13 -- both professionalize_llm and m2m100_418m are hallucinating/duplicating this ONE link into ~13 copies, not mistranslating it. All 4 wave25 pages carry the IDENTICAL See Also link (verified: gltf.md, profiles.md, render.md all end with the same 'Aspose.3D for .NET — Enterprise Documentation' line, same URL) -- a shared template-level link across the whole 3d/net product family, explaining the uniform 100% failure. Recurring REJECT across 4 independent, unrelated postpositional/particle languages (Hindi, Korean, Turkish -- caught by subagent review; Japanese -- found by my own direct read, not part of that review batch since ja is m2m-primary), all at the SAME structural position: the frontmatter `title` field only. Source: 'Aspose.BarCode for Python'. In every one of these 4 languages, the 'for'-equivalent postposition/particle (Hindi 'के लिए', Korean '용', Turkish 'için', Japanese '用') gets attached to the WRONG noun -- 'Aspose.BarCode <postposition> Python' instead of the grammatically correct 'Python <postposition> Aspose.BarCode' -- inverting the intended 'X for Y' relationship (reads roughly as 'Python for Aspose.BarCode'). CONFIRMED not isolated model variance: the SAME document's body and/or description sentence, translating the identical underlying relationship ('... for Python'), gets the postposition placement RIGHT in all 4 languages (e.g. ja body correctly has 'Python 用の', while the title has 'Aspose.BarCode 用 Python'). This means the title field is going through a DIFFERENT code path or losing context the body/description path has -- title is a short, isolated frontmatter string with no surrounding sentence structure, so the model has less signal for which noun the postposition should bind to. Preceding-preposition languages in the same wave (hu 'számára', ro 'pentru', and all Romance/Germanic/Arabic/CJK-non-particle locales in the earlier review) are unaffected -- this is specific to postpositional/particle grammars. TM purged (28 entries, hi/ko/tr/ja). Quarantining these 4 cells; shipping the other 21 (19 LLM + hu/ro m2m). NEXT: if this recurs on a second page, it meets the RECURRENCE ESCALATION bar (2+ pages) and a producer-side fix (likely: give the title-translation prompt/path explicit source-sentence context, or a title-specific postposition-order check) becomes mandatory before further Track-A work; on a single page it is a documented, ticketed, non-blocking quarantine.

REAL ROOT CAUSE found by reading src/workers/campaign_runner.py _frontmatter_source_guidance (the function that builds the retry-time instruction telling the model which source tokens to preserve vs translate): its stopwords set explicitly contains "for", and the substantive-word filter also requires len(token) >= 4, so "for" is excluded from BOTH the preserve-list and the explicit translate-list on every retry. For a title like "Aspose.PDF FOSS for Python", both neighbors of "for" ("FOSS" is all-caps, "Python" is in known_protected) are classified as protected tokens, leaving "for" as the ONLY ordinary word -- and the substantive-word list falls back to the generic literal string "all ordinary words" instead of ever naming it. The retry instruction the model actually received across all 3 attempts (professionalize_llm + 2x m2m100) never once said the word "for"; it only said "translate every other token" in the abstract. This explains why the retry loop, which is wired correctly for FrontmatterLanguageCheck failures and does carry retry_feedback through to the backend, still failed identically 3 times: the specific failing word was never named.

FIX (commit pending, see git log): _frontmatter_source_guidance now tracks stopword tokens positionally sandwiched between two protected/identifier tokens (both neighbors match the existing _is_identifier check) as "connectors", and when non-empty appends an explicit sentence: 'These preserved tokens are not a single fixed phrase: connector words between them, such as "for", are ordinary language and must still be translated ... not left in English.' Purely additive (only adds a sentence when a sandwiched stopword is found); does not change behavior for any other retry case. Covered by tests/regression/test_frontmatter_connector_word_retry_feedback.py (4 new tests, using the REAL pdf/python title text as fixture) plus the full existing tests/unit/workers/test_campaign_manifest.py (68 tests) and retry-feedback regression/unit suites (25 tests) all still green.

Nothing ever populated "suggestion" for this validator, and the issue .message itself (engine.py ~2208-2212) only ever said WHICH field failed and the similarity score, never WHAT TEXT was left over. CONFIRMED via direct TranslationEngine.translate_file() call (bypassing CampaignManifest.verify_environment, whose TM-fingerprint check is currently unwinnable -- the shared LMDB store is being written by peer campaigns faster than a manifest build+launch race can complete). This is a genuinely NEW defect class, not previously ticketed, discovered while investigating model_quality_residual_phrase_defects (TC-APT-102) -- this page has 2 fenced csharp code blocks, both containing the identical line "using Aspose.Words.Drawing.Charts;". BOTH blocks come back from translation as "using Aspose.Words.Drawing.Diagramme;" -- the C# namespace segment "Charts" (which must never be touched, it is inside a fenced code block) gets replaced with "Diagramme", the German translation of the word "Charts" as used LEGITIMATELY elsewhere on the same page as a markdown heading ("### Charts" -> correctly "### Diagramme"). The corruption is byte-identical across both code blocks (not independent per-call variance), which points to a deterministic lookup/substitution mechanism (most likely a Translation Memory hit keyed on the bare word, or a whole-document consistency/find-replace pass) rather than the LLM independently hallucinating the same wrong output twice. Confirmed NOT a reconstruction-stage bug: text_unit_extractor.py _extract_code_block (~line 1768) correctly creates code blocks as ONE do_not_translate=True unit with source_text=node.raw (the full verbatim code); ast_renderer.py renders CODE_BLOCK nodes from node.raw verbatim with no translation logic at all. So the leak happens somewhere between extraction and reconstruction -- dispatched a subagent to trace the exact mechanism in segment_translator.py / the TM layer (result not yet in when this ticket was opened).

BLAST RADIUS CONCERN (not yet measured): any page where a code identifier/namespace segment happens to share an EXACT word with translated prose elsewhere on the same page (e.g. "Table", "Document", "Page", "Form", "Color" -- all common English words that are also common C#/API identifiers) is a candidate for this same corruption. Given how common single-English-word class/namespace names are in Aspose's own API surface, this could be a meaningfully widespread, previously-undetected defect class -- StructureValidator only WARNS on code content mismatch today (not ERROR, see structure_validator.py _check_code_block_contents docstring: 'promotes to ERROR after production data shows <1% FP'), so it is plausible this exact corruption has been silently shipping in already-committed pages without being caught by the zero-defect gate battery as a hard rejection in some run configurations. This specific run DID reject on it under zero-defect policy (see data/campaigns/debug-codeblock-words-net-20260910/failure_metadata.jsonl and debug-codeblock3-words-net-20260910/, gate=StructureValidator) -- but worth confirming it always blocks and never silently passes in other configurations.

DO NOT attempt a fix until the subagent's root-cause trace lands and is read; this note exists so the confirmed reproduction is not lost if the investigation spans a session boundary.

Portfolio-wide blast-radius audit for TC-APT-109 (see manual-code-block-translation-leak-FIXED-VERIFIED), per the next-step noted when that ticket closed. Static, read-only, mechanical scan (no writes): for every git-tracked English source page, found headings (4+ chars, excluding code-block content -- first pass had a false-positive bug matching Python '# comment' lines as markdown headings, fixed before the real numbers below) whose exact text also appears as a whole word inside a fenced code block on the SAME page -- the precondition for the TC-APT-078 cross-reference-correction leak.

RESULT: 178 distinct pages portfolio-wide have this theoretical collision shape. Only 12 of those pages have any committed (git-tracked) translated sibling at all: 3d-java-scene-graph-materials, 3d-key-features (java), 3d-dotnet-primitives-mesh-ops, 3d-key-features-dotnet, introducing-aspose-note-foss-for-python, introducing-pdf-foss-cpp, go-pdf-create-merge-split, slides-visual-effects-{cpp,java,dotnet,python}, tex-engine-python (all under content/blog.aspose.org/).

For those 12, ran a STRICT byte-level verification: reconstruct what each colliding code block WOULD look like if _correct_cross_references had run (word-boundary substitute the source heading text with that file's own heading translation), and compare byte-for-byte against the actual committed sibling's code block at the same position. Zero-tolerance match required -- this rules out the two false-positive classes already found and ruled out during this audit: (a) source-code-sample drift (the English page's code was legitimately rewritten to a newer API after an older translation was committed -- produces wholesale, unrelated diffs, not a single surgical word substitution: found on words/python/introducing-words-foss-python, where source now uses doc.save() and the old German translation still shows the prior LdmMarkdownWriter().write() API -- unrelated to TC-APT-109, a separate staleness issue not investigated further here); (b) code comments matching the '# heading' regex pattern (fixed in the audit script itself before producing these numbers).

CONFIRMED RESULT: 0 of the 12 pages show any actual TC-APT-109 corruption in already-committed content. The bug, while real (confirmed live on words-foss-net) and now fixed (commit 57c6167a), does not appear to have visibly damaged any already-shipped page in the current portfolio -- most likely because the full precondition (a real markdown heading that both (1) actually translates away from its English source text in a given locale AND (2) has that exact English text recur verbatim inside a different code block on the same page AND (3) that locale is already committed) is a narrow enough intersection that it simply had not been hit yet in already-shipped work, even though it was hit immediately on the very next fresh page investigated (words-foss-net).
